claims.explanation: GW-583340 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling. Sensitive lines include those with EGFR mutations (HCC4006, NCIH1650) and other RTK/RAS pathway alterations, while resistant lines often have mutations in downstream effectors (e.g., BRAF, NRAS, NF1) or lack EGFR/ERBB2 addiction. High EGFR or ERBB2 expression, or activating mutations in these receptors, likely predicts sensitivity.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations predict response to EGFR inhibitors; observed in sensitive lines HCC4006 and NCIH1650.
ERBB2 is a direct target of GW-583340; overexpression may confer sensitivity.
High EGFR expression can increase dependence on EGFR signaling.
KRAS mutations may bypass EGFR dependence; observed in several resistant lines (e.g., CL11, MKN1).
BRAF mutations activate downstream MAPK, reducing reliance on EGFR; seen in resistant melanoma lines.
NRAS mutations activate MAPK independently of EGFR; observed in resistant lines KU1919 and IPC298.
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS, bypassing EGFR inhibition; frequent in resistant lines.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, potentially bypassing EGFR dependence; seen in resistant lines.
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K pathway, reducing reliance on EGFR; observed in resistant lines.
MAP2K1 mutations activate MEK, bypassing EGFR; seen in resistant line NCIH1437.
ERBB3 mutation may alter heterodimerization and signaling; observed in resistant line SNUC5.
MET amplification/mutation can bypass EGFR inhibition; seen in resistant line HGC27.
